name: Sheet 1 of 1
oneLine: A ruled specimen certificate that shows one real capability filled into every field an ISO 17025 certificate requires, beside the proficiency bar with every one of those fields printed as a dash, closed by a hatched SCOPE — NOT COVERED band carrying the real AWS/GCP row.
threeSecondRead: This is a form — a ruled sheet with numbered compartments and field captions — not the skills list I expected.
One compartment is filled in: a number, a place, a gold bracket on a name I could go and ask. The one next to it is a familiar grey bar whose every field reads '–'.
The hatched strip across the bottom is the part he is refusing to certify, and it is printed rather than omitted.
form:
A `<figure>` between the header and `<Bench>`, full inner width (78rem), replacing the 3-line lede outright.

**Title block.** One new mono line under `<h2>`: `CERTIFICATE 16b856c0 · ITEM UNDER TEST: VIKRAM DESHPANDE · SHEET 1 OF 1 · 17 ROWS` — 0.68rem `--font-mono`, tracking .12em, `--mist-400`, 1px `--token-border-default` rule beneath. Cert number is `cvFingerprint.short`.

**Figcaption first in DOM** (layer-cake): `--font-heading` clamp(1.05rem,1.6vw,1.35rem) `--white` — "Nothing here is self-rated." + a 0.9rem `--mist-200` body line.

**Frame.** 1px `--card-border`, `border-radius:0`, bg `rgb(244 246 250 / .015)`, padding clamp(1rem,2.5vw,1.75rem).

Row 0, 34px masthead, 1px bottom rule: a 28×14 SVG third-angle projection glyph (2 `<line>` groups, `--mist-400` 0.75, `crispEdges`), then `SPECIMEN · HOW ONE LINE IS READ` (9.5px mono, .14em, `--mist-400`); right-aligned `SHEET 1 OF 1 · CERT 16b856c0`.

Body grid `1.35fr 1fr`, gap 0, 1px column rule, padding clamp(.9rem,2vw,1.5rem).

**01 ITEM CALIBRATED.** Fields stacked, each on a hairline `rgb(255 255 255 / .05)` rule, caption 9.5px mono .14em `--mist-400`, boxed balloon numeral `01` (14px square, 1px `--ink-500`). Values, live from `capabilities[2]`: item `--font-body` .95rem `--white`; READING `--font-mono` .8rem `--mist-100` tabular-nums — `10,000+ concurrent devices held at P95 under 200 ms`; TAKEN AT wrapped in the existing `<Caliper state="sourced">ANZ Banking Group</Caliper>` — the figure's only gold — under it `PROGRAMME · VERIFY BY ASKING THE EMPLOYER`.

**02 INSTRUMENT NOT ACCEPTED.** One SVG, `viewBox 0 0 240 96`, `aspect-ratio` reserved, `aria-hidden`, **no `<path>`**: track `<rect x=8.5 y=20.5 w=223 h=14>` stroke `--ink-500` 1; fill `<rect w=156>` `--ink-500`; two 0.75 `--mist-400` extension lines dropping to y=52; a dimension line between them with 9×3 `<polygon>` arrowheads; in its break a `?` in `--font-heading` 13px — a dimension with no unit. Beneath, an HTML 2×2 mono grid, 8.5px: `NOMINAL –  UNCERTAINTY –  METHOD –  ISSUED BY –`. Footnote `*` .66rem: "Every field a certificate requires is empty here. A reader cannot check a length."

**03 SCOPE OF CALIBRATION — NOT COVERED.** Full-width band, min 64px, top rule, absolutely-positioned hatch layer: `<pattern id="skills-scope-hatch" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" width="10" height="10" patternTransform="rotate(45)">` one `<line>` `--ink-500` 0.5 — pitch deliberately unlike the Caliper's, per ISO 128-3 adjacent-body rule. On it: `<Caliper state="open">AWS and GCP certification</Caliper>`, then the row's real `evidence` and `caveat` strings.

Foot strip, mono .66rem `--mist-400`: `PROGRAMME — ask the employer · REPOSITORY — open it · CREDENTIAL — ask the issuer · 13 SOURCES`.

Card foot gains `END OF CERTIFICATE`, .62rem mono, .22em, `--mist-400`, above a 1px rule.
motion:
One beat, once, then dead — matching the section's written intent that it stay silent.

Trigger: `IntersectionObserver({threshold: 0.2})` on the figure, `observer.disconnect()` on first hit, sets `data-drawn`; `setTimeout(1000)` sets `data-settled`, which applies `animation: none` to every descendant (Bench's exact drawn/settled shape).

1. **120–576ms — the sheet rules itself.** Five hairlines (masthead, two field rules, column rule, scope-band top rule) are `<i>` elements animated `transform: scaleX(0)→1`, `transform-origin: left` (`scaleY`, origin top, for the column rule). 440ms `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` — a new `--motion-ease-mechanical` token, decelerating with **no overshoot**, because a caliper that bounces is a broken caliper. Stagger `calc(var(--i) * 34ms)` set inline. Compositor-only; `will-change: transform` added on trigger, removed at settled.

2. **460–780ms — the ink arrives.** `opacity: 0→1` only, 260ms `var(--motion-ease-emphasized)`, stagger 40ms, in this exact order: item → reading → the gold caliper closing on `ANZ Banking Group` → the grey bar and its dashes. Order is load-bearing (pratfall/blemishing): the measured evidence resolves before the discredited object.

3. **780–940ms — the scope band.** Hatch + open caliper fade in, 160ms linear, last. The admitted gap is the final thing to arrive and the thing that stays.

No `width`, no `clip-path`, no `filter`, no loop, no scroll-scrubbing, no scrolljack. Total 890ms; well inside the 3s budget and under the ≤2.4s ceiling.
states:
**Reduced motion.** Motion is authored as the enhancement, not an override: base CSS *is* the settled frame (rules at `scaleX(1)`, everything `opacity:1`); all keyframes live inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a missed selector fails static, not animated. Plus the JS branch from `Bench.tsx:189-207`: if `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`, set `drawn` and `settled` immediately and never observe. The global `animation-duration:.001ms !important` kill-switch is harmless because every end state is the true state. All three beats survive as simultaneous layout — the argument is identical, only its unfolding is gone.

**No JS.** Identical: everything is server-rendered HTML plus one static inline SVG. The only JS is the motion gate.

**390px.** Grid collapses to one column at ≤860px, order preserved: 01 → 02 → 03. Column rule becomes a horizontal rule. Projection glyph `display:none` below 480px. Captions 9px, item .9rem, reading .74rem mono with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`; the 240×96 SVG scales to container width and stays legible because it is four rects and three lines. Masthead wraps to two lines. ≈520px tall. Nothing here is a diagram pretending to be readable at phone width — every compartment is a text block plus one small drawing.

**Keyboard / SR.** The figure adds no interactive elements and no `role="status"` (TC-SKILL-07 stays at count 1). The rejected-bar SVG is `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"`; its meaning is carried by real adjacent DOM text — the `NOMINAL – / UNCERTAINTY – / METHOD – / ISSUED BY –` grid and the footnote — so a screen reader hears *why* it is rejected rather than a label duplicating a picture. The gold and open brackets are the existing `Caliper` component, which already speaks its state via `.gloss`. Reading order = DOM order = the credibility order (source before gap).

**CLS.** Everything is static markup; the SVG carries an explicit `viewBox` + `aspect-ratio`; the figure sits *outside* `.tableWrap`, so it never enters the table-floor measurement and cannot change height on a filter round-trip (TC-SKILL-06's ±1px holds).
coherence:
**Extends.** It is the same instrument grammar as the rest of the site, moved onto paper: hairline strokes, no fills, uppercase mono nomenclature, square corners, `crispEdges`. It reuses the site's one taught mark rather than adding a second — the `sourced` Caliper closes on `ANZ Banking Group`, the `open` Caliper stands in the scope band — so the reader spends zero new learning budget (R9). It reuses Bench's proven machinery wholesale: the drawn/settled two-flag pattern, the reduced-motion early return, literal SVG ids (`skills-scope-hatch`), inline `--i` custom properties.

**Deliberately avoids.** No dial, bezel, ring, tick-ring or index-at-twelve — About's Compass owns those. No proportional bar on a real axis, no gridlines, no decade ticks — Experience owns those, and the one bar here is explicitly a negated artifact with no axis and no unit. No node-link wires, rails or hover-dimming — the Bench already spends those, and it sits directly beneath, untouched. No box-and-arrow flow, no pipeline, no literal drawn caliper mechanism — Vitrine owns those. No seal, ribbon, scroll or stamp: this draws what a certificate *does*, not what one looks like in stock art. No WebGL (TC-CINE-04), no `<path>` anywhere (TC-BENCH-01/02 keep passing at 20 and 17 unchanged).

**Gold.** Exactly one gold object in the entire figure, and it arrives through `Caliper.module.css` — no new hex, nothing for the MONO gate to catch. It sits on `ANZ Banking Group`, which is a checkable programme: gold means "there is a source you can go and check", and here it is drawn as the terminator of a traceability field rather than a path, a fill, a theme or a highlight. The grey bar gets none; the hatch gets none; the rules get none. That the empty compartment cannot earn gold *is* the lesson, so palette rule and argument reinforce each other instead of competing. MONO-05's requirement that gold render inside `#skills` is unaffected — the table's production glyphs are untouched.

**Build hazards to respect.** New CSS goes in a module, never `globals.css` (DEADCSS). No comment may contain "mock", "stub", "TODO" (TC-NFR-COMPLETE is line-level and includes comments). All micro-captions use `--mist-400`, not `--ink-300`, which fails 4.5:1 at these sizes.
risks: Density. It is a lot of 9-10px mono in one frame. If the compartment captions are set too tight or too dim it stops being a certificate and becomes visual noise, and the 7-second scan is lost to a second reading. Mitigation is ruthless: four field captions in compartment 01, four dashes in 02, one caption in 03 — no more. If it needs a fifth field it is wrong.

The grey bar can be misread as a claim about him rather than about the convention. It sits under a caption reading INSTRUMENT NOT ACCEPTED and beside four printed dashes, but a skimmer who reads only shapes could take away 'he is 70% at something'. If user testing shows that, the fill drops from 156 to ~90 units so it reads as an obviously arbitrary length, or the fill is removed entirely and only the empty track remains.

Two hatch pitches in one section (this band at 10px, the Caliper's own behind its value) can moire on some scalings, and would look like a rendering bug rather than the ISO 128-3 adjacent-body convention it is. Needs checking at 1x, 1.5x, 2x DPR before it ships.

Tone drift. The masthead line and END OF CERTIFICATE are one sentence away from pastiche — a fake accreditation number, a fake signatory, a fake 'UKAS' badge would instantly turn the whole section into cosplay and destroy the credibility it exists to buy. Every field must be a real fact or it must not be printed. The cert number is a genuine MD5 of a PDF the reader can download and hash.

It absorbs the lede, so if the figure fails to render for any reason the section loses its only explanation of the metaphor. The figcaption must therefore be plain text outside the SVG and outside any measured container, so it survives every failure mode including no CSS.

Three compartments plus a masthead is close to the ceiling of what can be introduced in one frame. If the entrance stagger is lengthened or a fourth compartment is added, it crosses from 'one specimen explained' into a second diagram that competes with the Bench sitting 40px below it.
whyBest:
It is the only concept that answers all three visitor questions with one object and no argument. The competing approaches each answer one: a vernier-coincidence animation teaches what calibration *is* but never says why the bars are gone; a traceability ladder shows provenance but duplicates the Bench directly beneath it; a guard-band diagram is a beautiful chart that a non-metrologist cannot read in three seconds. A filled-in form beside an empty one needs no vocabulary at all — the reader already knows what an unfilled field means.

It is diagnostically correct. The section's measured failure is split attention: the metaphor lives in a prose lede physically separated from the artefact it names. This does not add explanation, it *deletes* the explanation and moves it onto the object, which is what every pattern in the editorial research converges on.

It is the assigned angle pushed to its end. The header becomes a title block, the figure is the specimen entry, the card foot closes with an end-of-certificate marker. The whole of §4 stops being a table with a metaphorical title and becomes one document with a beginning, a numbered body and a closure — which is precisely why a real certificate reads as authoritative rather than decorative.

It exploits the one thing no portfolio has. Certificates persuade because of the field for what was not tested. That field already exists as data — the pending AWS/GCP row with its real caveat — and it is currently buried at the bottom of a 17-row table where nobody reads it. Promoting it into a hatched band with real area, arriving last, is the pratfall effect executed correctly: competence first, admitted limit second, and the limit given enough geometric space to actually be perceived.

Finally, it is the cheapest safe build on the board. Zero new dependencies, zero new hex, zero new `<path>` elements so the existing bench assertions hold untouched, no canvas, no scroll coupling, no measured geometry, no interaction. Roughly 200 lines of TSX and CSS reusing two components and one proven motion pattern, sitting outside every measured container in the section.
